dialog.body: Public Works, this is Kevin.

Yes, hello, Kevin. My name is Elvis Gomes, and I want to give you a little background first so you understand. I rent the downstairs at the house, I've been there going on eleven years, and there's a driveway we share with the neighbor, the one next door, it runs along the side. Now I don't drive much anymore, but my niece takes me to my appointments, and she has to pull in there. So the thing is, the plow came by and left a berm across the end of the driveway.
Okay, a berm across the driveway. Got it. And where are you located, Mr. Gomes?

89 Callender Avenue. That's up the North End, not far from the corner. Kevin, I'll tell you, it's been three days. The storm was Sunday into Monday, the snow-to-rain one, and it started as snow, then turned to rain, and everything froze up solid after. So that pile the plow left is not fluffy. It's like concrete.

Yeah, that's the worst kind. The heavy wet stuff that sets up overnight. Let me write this down. Eighty-nine Callender, plow berm blocking the shared driveway, left from Monday's storm. Is the street itself plowed okay?

The street is fine, the street is plowed fine. It's just that at the bottom of the driveway they push it all right across. I went out with the shovel Tuesday, and I did about ten minutes and I had to stop. I'm seventy-some years old, I'm not lifting ice. And the neighbor, he's got a bad back, so he's not doing it either.
Understood. So nobody's been able to get a car in or out.

Right, right. My niece parked on the street Wednesday and walked in, and it's not safe, she's slipping the whole way. Which brings me to the other thing. The walkway and the driveway, it's all glazed over. Can I get some sand? Do you give out sand, or do you bring it? I don't know how it works.

We do have sand. Usually there's a pile residents can grab from, and you bring your own bucket or bag. I can check which location is closest to you. If you can't get there, I can put in a note for a sand request at the address. Can you carry a bucket, or is that out too?
A bucket I can do. A small one. I just can't do a whole shovel of it, you know. But how would I get there? Like I said, I don't drive.

Yeah, fair. Let me do this. I'll put in the request for sand to be dropped at the address and I'll flag the berm for a crew. I can't tell you what day, they're still working through a backlog from the storm. But it'll be on the list with your name.
A backlog, three days. Well. I'm not blaming you, Kevin, you're the one who answered. It's just, they plow it in, and then they leave it. You'd think the plow guy would notice a driveway.

I hear you. Sometimes it's the truck just pushing what's in front of it, and he doesn't see the driveway at all. But it's a fair thing to ask. And is it only your end that's blocked, or the whole width?

The whole width. Wall to wall, basically. Maybe two feet high, and about as wide as a car. And there's a lump of ice in the middle that I think is a chunk off the plow itself, or something, I don't know.
Okay. Whole width, about two feet high, iced over. I've got that. And a callback number in case the crew needs to reach you?
It's 401-555-0179. That's the landline, so if I don't pick up, let it ring, because I'm slow getting to the phone. The cord doesn't reach the kitchen.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-seven-nine. Got it. I'll note to let it ring.

Thank you. Now, this is a little off the subject, so forgive me. But since I'm stuck inside, I've been writing. I do short stories, just for myself, I've done it for years. And right now I'm stuck on an ending. I've got a man who shovels out a driveway for a neighbor, and I can't figure out how it ends. I've been sitting at the table since Tuesday.
Well, maybe the berm gets you an ending. Plow comes, problem solved. That's a happy one.
If only. It's not that kind of story, Kevin. Anyway. I'll let you go. You'll send the sand?

I've got it in as a sand request plus the berm. I can't give you a time, but it's logged for 89 Callender, and they'll call that number if they need anything. If it's still sitting there Monday, give us a call back and we'll push it.
Monday. All right. I'll be here. Thank you.
You're welcome, Mr. Gomes. Stay off that ice in the meantime.
I will. Goodbye.
